thread:
Mira: Hey @channel — quick question about first PRs: what's our preferred branching pattern and any hard limits on PR size? I'm about to open a change that touches routing + a small test.

Olivia: Welcome Mira! Branching: feature/<ticket> or fix/<ticket>. Keep PRs focused; aim for small, reviewable chunks. If it's >500 lines call it out in the PR description.

Sam: +1. Tag 2 reviewers where possible — area owner + a peer. Use CODEOWNERS to find owners; if unsure ping me.

Alex: Commit message convention: <scope>: short summary (e.g., runtime: reduce kv-cache allocs). Squash on merge is fine unless the history is meaningful.

Mira: Thanks! Are pre-commit hooks enforced in CI? My lint fails locally.

ci-bot: Running pre-commit hooks for Mira's branch... black/isort/flake8 -> blocking. See CI: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/1735551234 

Olivia: CI will block merges on lint/test failures. Easiest is `pre-commit run --all-files` or `make dev-setup` to install hooks. We also have a helper: `scripts/fix-style.sh` for common fixes.

Mira: Got it. Any expectations on tests? Unit only? Integration?

Sam: Unit tests required. Add a small integration test if you change networking or runtime behavior. Keep test fixtures small — mocks are fine. If you'd like I can pair-review the tests.

Mira: What's the canonical git flow for a feature? Example commands?

Alex: Typical:```bash
git checkout -b feature/XYZ-123-short-desc
# make changes
make test # runs unit tests locally
pre-commit run --all-files
git add -A && git commit -m "runtime: optimize kv cache"
git push --set-upstream origin feature/XYZ-123-short-desc
```

Sam: Add the ticket number in the branch and PR title. Use labels: `area/runtime`, `needs-review`. If CI is flaky, add `flake` label and mention @eng-oncall.

Mira: Any pitfalls I should watch for (generated files, big diffs)?

Alex: Don't commit generated artifacts in gen/ unless you're changing the schema. Watch for large binary diffs (check `git status --porcelain`) and use `git add -p`.

Olivia: Also check CODEOWNERS for mandatory reviewers. For infra/runtime changes, ping @Alex and @Sam explicitly in the PR body and include a short rollout plan (how to revert if perf regresses).

Mira: Who gives the final approval on runtime area?

Sam: Owners listed in CODEOWNERS are the final approvers. For anything risky or with perf implications, we do an extra perf sign-off (usually me + Alex). For infra-wide changes, open a short RFC in #architecture first.

Mira: Perfect — that's super helpful. I'll open the PR now and ping you both for reviews. TY :heart:

ci-bot: Build passed ✅ (tests: 124/124) on branch feature/XYZ-123-short-desc

Olivia: Nice! Drop the PR link here when you open it and we'll take a look. :thumbsup:
